transcript:
[00:00] Meeting header: 2026-02-28 15:00 PST | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Samir Khan (Redwood AE), Elena Park (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Vela CTO), Marco Li (Eng Manager), Priya Nair (Platform)

[00:12] Samir (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro i'm samir, i'm the AE, with elena on the se side. how's everyone doing?
[00:20] Aisha (Vela): good, thanks. busy quarter but excited to chat about your quickstart and what we can do with the hosted api first.
[00:30] Samir: great. high level: today we want to understand your use cases, constraints, and timeline. we'll cover the self-serve quickstart, free credits, and options if you scale to dedicated or private later.
[00:45] Elena (Redwood SE): and i'll walk through a super small integration path  basically time-to-first-token: how fast you can demo in your app, and what infra we recommend.
[00:55] Marco: perfect. real quick context: we're building a chat+semantic search feature in our product. initial rollout to internal users then a public beta. priority is latency for UX, and not leaking customer data  some of our customers have residency requirements.
[01:12] Priya: our infra is in AWS us-west-2, we use k8s, and we have an internal ml infra team. for the pilot we want a low friction path, ideally self-serve.
[01:25] Samir: makes sense. typical approach: start with hosted api + free credits for quick experiments, then move to dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and private (VPC/on-prem) if you need strict data residency or air-gapped.
[01:40] Aisha: question on the free credits are those per team? how long do they last?
[01:48] Samir: yes, we offer trial credits for new accounts tied to the org. generally enough to run through a quickstart and a small pilot we'll put specifics in the email. they expire in 30 days usually.
[01:59] Elena: for time-to-first-token, you can get a demo running in under 20 minutes if you use our quickstart: create an api key, use the curl or node snippet we provide, and plug into your frontend. the big gotcha is prompt engineering and initial model selection.
[02:15] Marco: about latency what kind of p50/p99 numbers should we expect on hosted? our UX target is ~200ms for short responses.
[02:26] Elena: p50s for short generation on our hosted prod are often 80-150ms depending on model; p99 can be several 100s. for strict targets, dedicated capacity gives you stronger SLOs. we also surface token-level breakdowns in the console so you can reason about cost/latency tradeoffs.
[02:45] Aisha: earlier you mentioned caching and batching does that affect freshness for chat?
[02:51] Elena: good callout prefix/KV caching helps for repeated prefixes (like system prompts) and speeds up warm requests; for fresh user messages we avoid caching that would leak data, but we do a lot with batching and kv cache management on the runtime to reduce cost without impacting correctness.
[03:10] Priya: security checklist do you have SOC2 and support for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
[03:18] Samir: we are SOC2 compliant and we offer KMS integrations for Private deployments. For Hosted, keys at rest are encrypted, and we provide audit logs; we can share the security pack and SOC2 report after an NDA if needed.
[03:32] Aisha: is the private option a full on-prem package or VPC peering?
[03:36] Elena: both. Private can be a VPC-connected control plane with customer-managed networking, or an on-prem bundle for air-gapped requirements. depends on the compliance needs and timeline.
[03:50] Marco: timeline if we start with hosted self-serve quickstart this week, what's the path to a pilot?
[03:57] Samir: common pattern: day 0-7 quickstart and integration with free credits and sample prompts; week 2 run internal pilot and small benchmark; by week 4 decide whether to stay hosted or move to dedicated. we can help with a small benchmark and an eval harness.
[04:15] Priya: for the benchmark, what's the recommended load profile?
[04:19] Elena: start with representative prompts and sequence lengths. we'll give you a checklist: 1) typical prompt lengths, 2) p95 latency targets, 3) concurrency targets. we'll also suggest quantization/model profiles if cost is a concern.
[04:33] Aisha: pricing do you have a per-token cost chart? we need predictable unit economics for the pilot.
[04:40] Samir: yes, hosted pricing is usage-based; dedicated has reserved monthly commits with lower unit costs. i'll include sample numbers tailored to expected qps for chat.
[04:52] Marco: any gotchas on SDKs? we use node and go.
[04:56] Elena: we have official SDKs for node, python, and simple curl examples for go. the main thing is streaming vs non-streaming for your UX. streaming gets lower perceived latency.
[05:10] [Speaker overlap / crosstalk] Aisha: and encryption in transit?
[05:14] Samir: TLS in transit, at-rest encryption; for hosted we manage keys, for private you can bring your own KMS.
[05:25] Marco: competitor question how do you compare to openai or anthro-.. anthrophic?
[05:31] Samir: a lot of teams start with the big hosted providers; our diff is production-first inference tooling, transparent perf profiles, and an easier path to dedicated/private without redoing integrations.
[05:45] Priya: curious about running LLMs inside our VPC and if we can control versions for rollouts.
[05:51] Elena: yes, private gives you a control plane where you can pin model versions and rollout policies. dedicated also supports pinned variants and can be configured for canaries.
[06:05] Aisha: ok this is helpful. for the quickstart could you share a minimal example for time-to-first-token  like from repo to demo in 15 minutes?
[06:15] Elena: absolutely. we'll share a quickstart repo link and a node snippet: npm install @redwood/inference, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run the snippet. usually under 20 min.
[06:27] Samir: we'll include the exact curl and sdk snippets, plus a step-by-step playbook link: https://redwood.ai/quickstart-playbook (playbook url placeholder).
[06:39] Marco: any limitations on data logs retention for hosted? we need 90 days retention for debug logs.
[06:46] Samir: hosted retains logs for 30 days by default; we offer extended retention as an add-on, and enterprise plans can configure longer retention or ship logs to your SIEM.
[06:58] Aisha: on data residency, if some of our users are in eu we need eu-hosted region. do you support region pins?
[07:05] Elena: yes, we have regions in na and eu, and we can route traffic by region. private deployments are used if you need stricter residency.
[07:18] Priya: one more technical does the runtime support kv cache and long context? we plan to have histories up to 8k tokens.
[07:25] Elena: yes, runtime supports kv cache management and optimized kernels for longer context. we can discuss quantization if you want to reduce memory.
[07:38] [10 min silence / background] Aisha: ok let's talk next steps.
[07:46] Samir: recap: we'll send quickstart playbook + free credits, elena will send benchmark checklist and minimal sdk/curl snippets. you'll share compliance requirements and confirm pilot scope.
[07:58] Marco: can we get a small POC of 1k requests at 50 rps to test p95?
[08:04] Elena: yes we can run that; please send sample prompts and target seq lengths.
[08:10] Aisha: thanks everyone, this was super useful.
[08:14] Samir: thanks all, i'll follow up with the email.

End of transcript
